summary: The paper presents an exemplary machine-checked formalization and exact-rational certificate auditing framework for Randall Shaw's canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem. Using an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel and a pure-stdlib zero-float Python verifier spanning 16 canonical certificates, the work rigorously establishes similarity scaling, homothety obstruction rescues via rational rotations, subspace-equivalence, and inductive union bounds while successfully defending against 57 adversarial forgeries.
weaknesses: Scope is strictly bounded to the finite algebraic, similarity-geometric, and probabilistic union-bound core, excluding the infinite-grid DGPV Ramsey theorem and arbitrary irrational point sets in R^d.
